qa.name: Biceps Brachii — Long Head
qa.function: Flexion of the elbow, supination of the forearm, weak flexion of the shoulder
qa.clinical_note: Long head tendon travels through the intertubercular groove — a common site of tendinitis and rupture causing a Popeye deformity

qa.name: Biceps Brachii — Short Head
qa.function: Flexion of the elbow, supination of the forearm, adduction of the arm
qa.clinical_note: Shares origin with coracobrachialis at the coracoid process — both are innervated by the musculocutaneous nerve

qa.name: Brachialis
qa.origin: Distal half of the anterior surface of the humerus
qa.insertion: Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna
qa.innervation: Musculocutaneous nerve, small contribution from radial nerve
qa.function: Flexion of the elbow in all positions — the workhorse flexor of the elbow
qa.clinical_note: Inserts on the ulna so it is always a pure elbow flexor regardless of forearm pronation or supination — unlike biceps brachii

qa.name: Coracobrachialis
qa.insertion: Middle third of the medial surface of the humerus
qa.function: Flexion and adduction of the arm at the glenohumeral joint
qa.clinical_note: The musculocutaneous nerve pierces coracobrachialis — entrapment here causes weakness of elbow flexion and loss of lateral forearm sensation

qa.name: Triceps Brachii — Long Head
qa.function: Extension of the elbow, extension and adduction of the arm at the shoulder
qa.clinical_note: Only head of triceps that crosses the shoulder joint — can extend and adduct the arm; radial nerve injury causes wrist drop

qa.name: Triceps Brachii — Lateral Head
qa.origin: Posterior surface of the humerus superior to the radial groove
qa.clinical_note: Forms the lateral surface of the posterior arm — the most visible head during elbow extension against resistance

qa.name: Triceps Brachii — Medial Head
qa.origin: Posterior surface of the humerus inferior to the radial groove
qa.function: Extension of the elbow — the primary workhorse head of the triceps
qa.clinical_note: Deepest and most active head — active in all elbow extension; the lateral and long heads are recruited for forceful extension

qa.name: Anconeus
qa.insertion: Lateral surface of the olecranon and proximal posterior ulna
qa.function: Assists triceps in elbow extension, stabilizes the elbow joint, abducts the ulna during pronation
qa.blood_supply: Posterior interosseous artery, Deep brachial artery
qa.clinical_note: Small triangular muscle considered a continuation of the medial head of triceps — used as a surgical landmark at the lateral elbow
